title: Stack Profile Frontmatter
description: Schema for the YAML frontmatter of plugins/<name>/stack.md files. The frontmatter is extracted from between the first --- markers and validated as a JSON object.

allOf.description: Every profile must say how it is detected: stack providers (foundations) use `detect` (project structure); additive framework providers normally use `dependency` (the FOUNDATION that owns their aspect declares WHERE to search via its `framework_detection`; the orchestrator executes it) but may use `detect` as an escape hatch.

then.description: Additive (framework) profiles must not declare a workflow. They enrich existing phases; they do not own the pipeline.

Additive (framework) profiles must not declare `framework_detection` — hosting frameworks is a foundation's job. A framework is a leaf in the foundation→framework tree; it does not host other frameworks.

Additive (framework) profiles must not declare `hosts_aspects` — accepting frameworks is a foundation's job. A framework declares the single `enriches_aspect` it belongs to; it does not host categories.
The `dependency` shorthand is only for additive framework providers — a stack provider detects by project structure via `detect`.

stack.description: Unique stack name. Lowercase, alphanumeric + hyphens.

priority.description: 0 = vanilla fallback. 100+ = stack provider. Higher wins per aspect. For additive (framework) profiles this is documentational only — additive profiles never compete for an aspect.

additive.description: When true, this is an ADDITIVE (framework) profile: it contributes convention_skills, phase_prompts_injection, extra_phases, and post_pipeline_checks to the merge but is EXCLUDED from per-aspect winner resolution and from PRIMARY_PROFILE selection. Additive profiles MUST NOT declare agents_per_phase or a workflow — they enrich existing agents, they do not own phases. Defaults to false.

dependency.description: Framework providers ONLY: the library coordinate(s) that signal this framework is in use — e.g. 'com.squareup.retrofit2' (group) or 'com.squareup.retrofit2:retrofit' (group:artifact). The plugin just NAMES the dependency; the FOUNDATION that owns this framework's `enriches_aspect` declares WHERE to look (its `framework_detection`), and the orchestrator executes that search (version catalog first, then module build files). Prefer this over a hand-written `detect` block. A list matches if ANY coordinate is found.

aspects.description: PLATFORM / WINNER aspects this profile OWNS — the axis used for per-aspect winner resolution (which stack drives a part of the app: `android` for the foundation; `backend`/`frontend`/… for web stacks). This is NOT the functional library taxonomy (see `enriches_aspect` / `hosts_aspects`). Additive (framework) profiles use [] — they own no platform aspect.

enriches_aspect.description: Additive (framework) profiles ONLY: the FUNCTIONAL aspect this framework decorates — its library category (network, persistence, di, ui, background, analytics, architecture), NOT a platform. It is the contract that replaces any plugin→plugin install dependency: the framework attaches under whichever FOUNDATION declares it HOSTS this functional aspect (`hosts_aspects`), no specific plugin named. Frameworks own no platform aspect (`aspects: []`) but enrich one functional aspect. Omit on stack providers.

hosts_aspects.description: Stack providers (foundations) ONLY: the FUNCTIONAL aspects this foundation accepts frameworks for. A framework attaches here when its `enriches_aspect` is in this list AND its `dependency` is found via `framework_detection`. This is the foundation's explicit vouch ('I can mount a network/persistence/di/… framework into my phases') — adding a framework whose category is already listed needs zero edits here. Omit on additive profiles.

framework_detection.description: Stack providers (foundations) ONLY: the ordered list of files/globs where the orchestrator searches for a framework's `dependency` coordinate, ON THIS FOUNDATION'S BEHALF (0b-frameworks). The foundation owns WHERE to look (e.g. ['gradle/libs.versions.toml','**/build.gradle.kts','**/build.gradle']); the core owns only the substring-matching mechanics. Pairs with `hosts_aspects` (which functional categories) to define what this foundation hosts. A non-Gradle foundation lists entirely different locations and needs no core change. Omit on additive profiles.

workflow.description: Optional. Default workflow recipe this profile selects when it is the PRIMARY profile and neither --workflow=NAME nor sdlc.local.yaml active_workflow is given. Names a workflow recipe (e.g. 'android-feature'). Generic — any profile may declare one.

detect.description: Auto-detect rules. Use `any` for OR, `all` for AND.

platformAspect.description: PLATFORM / WINNER aspect — what a STACK PROVIDER owns and competes to win (which stack drives a part of the app). Used by `aspects`.

functionalAspect.description: FUNCTIONAL / LIBRARY aspect — the cross-cutting category a FRAMEWORK addresses. Used by `enriches_aspect` (one per framework) and `hosts_aspects` (a foundation's accepted set).

file_exists.description: Path (relative to project root) that must exist.

path.description: Path relative to project root. May be a glob (e.g. '**/build.gradle') — if it contains glob characters, the rule matches when ANY globbed file contains the pattern. Glob honors .gitignore.

pattern.description: Regex evaluated against the file contents.

file_glob.description: Glob pattern (relative to project root, e.g. '**/*.kt', '**/build.gradle*'). Matches if at least one file matches. Evaluated with the Glob tool — use for variable-named or nested artifacts (monorepo subtrees, module-level build files).

oneOf.description: Nested OR — matches if any sub-rule matches. Lets a profile compose rules, e.g. '(.kts OR .gradle) AND has Kotlin'.
Nested AND — matches only if every sub-rule matches.
